title: Flatness descends to one stage of a directed preorder
statement: Let I be a directed preorder and R:I -> CommRing a diagram of Noetherian rings. Let c be a limiting cone on R.op followed by Spec, with affine vertex. Fix i in I, a finitely presented morphism f:Xi -> Spec(R_i) [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], and a finitely presented O_Xi-module M [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. If the tensor pullback of M [def-pc-module-pullback] to the canonical fibre product Xi times Spec(R_i) c.pt [def-pc-base-change] is flat over c.pt [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], then there exist j in I and hij:i <= j such that the canonical pullback of M to Xi times Spec(R_i) Spec(R_j) is flat over Spec(R_j). Only one stage is asserted, not all later stages or arbitrary cartesian models.

proof.text: Construct J = I times the natural numbers, ordered by a = b or by a.first <= b.first and a.second < b.second. Equality gives reflexivity; transitivity follows from transitivity of <= and <; strict increase of the level rules out two opposite nonidentity inequalities, giving antisymmetry. A directed upper bound of the first coordinates with level max(a.second,b.second)+1 gives a directed upper bound in J. The projection p:J -> I is monotone and surjective. Mathlib Monotone.final_functor_iff proves its functor F final. Fix t = (i,0), so F(t) is definitionally i. This is a direct specialization of the directed replacement construction, with its properties proved locally; no choice of a module or new geometric object is needed.

Restrict R along F and c along F.op. By initiality of F.op and Mathlib Functor.Initial.isLimitWhiskerEquiv the restricted cone remains limiting, with exactly the same affine vertex. Its component at t is definitionally the component of c at i. All Noetherian hypotheses restrict pointwise. The finitely presented morphism f and module M are unchanged, and M is quasi-coherent by the existing IsFinitePresentation instance. Thus the original limit-flatness hypothesis is exactly the restricted hypothesis.

Apply partial-order eventual flat-module descent to F composed with R, the restricted cone, and t, f, M. Obtain s >= t and flatness at every stage above s. Specialize to s itself by reflexivity. Take j = F(s) and i <= j from monotonicity of the projection. By definition of functor composition and the thin-category morphisms, this stage is exactly the canonical base change required by the conclusion. No iterated pullback or cartesian-model comparison is used.

proof_origin.place: Concrete directed partial-order replacement with a fixed preimage of i; initial reindexing; specialize eventual descent to its first stage
proof_origin.note: X3 proves the auxiliary order and its final projection directly. The geometric flatness theorem remains the planned Tag 05LY dependency.

theorem exists_isFlatOver_of_isPullback_limit_preorder_stage
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [∀ k : I, IsNoetherianRing (R.obj k)]
    (c : Cone (R.op ⋙ Scheme.Spec)) (hc : IsLimit c) [IsAffine c.pt]
    (i : I) {Xi : Scheme.{u}} (f : Xi ⟶ Spec (R.obj i))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (M : Xi.Modules) [M.IsFinitePresentation]
    (hflat : ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback
      (pullback.fst f (c.π.app (op i)))).obj M).IsFlatOver
      (pullback.snd f (c.π.app (op i)))) :
    ∃ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j),
      ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback
        (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))).obj M).IsFlatOver
        (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
